text:
Brock Boeser has a point in 11 straight games (4 goals, 12 assists). In the 4-3 shootout win over Minnesota on Nov. 21 he set up three goals, including Marco Rossi's late tying goal, as Daniel Wagner noted. He has 28 points in 26 games, 18 of them on the power play, and his ice time is up 3:05 a night over his last ten, to 21:35.

What's driving it is the power play and the minutes, not five on five. At even strength Vancouver gets only 35.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 5.2 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, partly because his teammates rated among the weakest in the league by impact (bottom 6%).

Some of the scoring is borrowed, too. He's shooting 18.2% against a talent we put near 14%, and Vancouver has scored 4.6 more goals than expected with him on. The streak is a bright spot in a hard Canucks season; whether they can keep the puck when he's out at five on five is the bigger question.
